patch.value:
## Problem
The repository enforces literal 100 percent all-source coverage. That gate proves every line and branch was executed by the suite. It does not prove any of them were asserted on. A test that calls a function and ignores the result contributes full coverage and zero defect detection.

## Approach
Introduce mutation testing scoped first to the SDK core — the surface with the strongest correctness obligations and the most downstream consumers — then extend outward. Treat the score exactly like the existing static-quality ratchets: a floor that only moves up.

## Cost control
Mutation testing is expensive. Scope by module, run incrementally against changed files on pull requests and fully on the nightly schedule, and keep the pull-request path fast.

## Boundary
Not a replacement for the coverage gate. Not a rewrite of the suite. Surviving-mutant triage produces assertions, not deleted tests.
Mutation-testing gate: prove the 100 percent coverage suite actually detects defects, with a ratcheted mutation score on SDK core

A mutation-testing run produces a reproducible score for the SDK core module set in CI; The score is ratcheted: regressions fail, improvements move the floor, matching the existing suppressions-ratchet discipline; Runtime is bounded — incremental or partitioned execution keeps the gate inside the nightly budget rather than the pull-request budget if necessary; Surviving mutants are triaged with either a new assertion or a written equivalent-mutant waiver; no blanket ignores
Coverage stops being a proxy for test strength and becomes a measured property
Literal 100 percent all-source coverage is enforced, but coverage only proves lines executed — it cannot distinguish an assertion from a bare call. Mutation score measures what coverage claims.
Closes the largest blind spot in the quality gates: a suite can be fully green, fully covering, and still miss an entire class of introduced defects.
A mutation score baseline exists for the SDK core with a ratchet that fails CI on regression, and surviving mutants are triaged into either new assertions or recorded equivalent-mutant waivers.
The coverage ADR settled the coverage question; the next honest question is assertion strength, and it is cheapest to baseline before the SDK promotion partition finishes moving code.

value.text: Coverage-pragma density measured 2026-07-25, relevant to whether the 100% literal all-src number proves defect detection. 465 v8/c8/istanbul ignore pragmas exist across src, scripts and packages against the static-quality-gate ceiling MAX_COVERAGE_IGNORE_PRAGMAS = 496, i.e. 94% of the budget is consumed. They concentrate in exactly the largest and most complex files: src/sdk/governance/validate.ts 65, src/cli/main.ts 51, src/cli/commands/create.ts 37, src/sdk/governance/health.ts 25, src/sdk/extension.ts 24, src/sdk/test/execution.ts 22, src/cli/commands/contracts.ts 22, src/sdk/query/search.ts 21, src/sdk/history-redact.ts 21. vitest.config.ts excludes only src/**/*.d.ts, so the 100% figure is genuine for everything not pragma-excluded — which makes the pragma set, not the config, the real coverage boundary. A mutation score computed over SDK core should treat these regions explicitly: they are the places where surviving mutants are most likely and least visible. The ceiling is also a ceiling only, not a ratchet, so the count can grow to 496 without any gate reacting.
